Offices & mixed-use buildings

THE BRIEF

An occupied office needs its working areas, meeting rooms and visitor routes considered before attendance. We identify the defects and the people responsible for approvals, then separate local repairs from layout changes, a tenancy refresh or make-good work.

✺

PROPERTY IN USE

Work across the occupied floor

  • Rooms and finishes

    We scope meeting-room doors, wall damage, ceiling defects, fixed joinery and reception fittings. A water-stained ceiling is considered alongside the relevant source investigation.

  • Services and amenities

    Agreed lighting, air-conditioning and amenity work is listed by the area served. We identify which occupants and shared facilities are affected by any interruption.

  • Tenancy changes

    For local alterations and make-good, we distinguish retained fittings, removals, service coordination and final finishes against the agreed brief.

PROPERTY IN USE

Arrange the work around occupied areas

  1. 01

    Agree the operating window

    We check meeting schedules, staffed areas, visitor access, keys and any building-management conditions affecting the work.

  2. 02

    Prepare the route and protection

    Material deliveries, lifts, furniture protection, dust and waste movement are planned with the nominated contact.

  3. 03

    Return areas in stages

    We identify the completed rooms or zones and any remaining drying, testing or follow-up condition before normal use resumes.

PROPERTY IN USE

A coordinated finish across the floor

Ceiling tile sizes, partition details, hardware models and paint or laminate finishes are recorded where they affect the repair. We explain whether a local patch, a larger finish area or a replacement part is included.

The quote separates investigation, defined repairs and optional changes. Access restrictions, the number of rooms, finish matching and repeated attendance can all change the work package.

PROPERTY IN USE

What to include in the enquiry

  • A location-based list

    Mark the floor, room or shared area and describe the problem. Include photographs and any relevant equipment or finish details.

  • People and timing

    Identify the tenant or property representative, the available work windows and any move-in or handover date.

PROPERTY IN USE

Records for tenants and property teams

We list completed work by room or zone, record the checks relevant to the task and identify any outstanding decision. A shared-area repair and a tenant-specific item remain separately traceable in the handover.

A FEW GOOD QUESTIONS

Good to know.

Can an occupied office be updated in sections?+

We assess the work boundaries, service connections and routes, then agree a sequence by room or zone. Tasks that affect several areas are identified before the staging plan is confirmed.

Do you need a full design for a small repair list?+

A clear location list and photographs can start the enquiry. We identify where measurements, equipment details or an approved alteration brief are needed before defining those items.
